title: Chili
summary: Texas-born stew of meat and chiles — beans debate included.
origins: Chili con carne emerges from San Antonio's chili queens street vendors in the late 1800s — a working-class Tex-Mex market food, not a Mexican import. The International Chili Society and Texas purists insist on no beans; Midwest home cooks often add kidney beans anyway.
history: Chili spread via cattle trails and World's Fair booths (1893 Chicago). Canned chili (1920s) and chili powder blends made it a national pantry meal. Regional forks include Cincinnati five-way, New Mexico green chile stew, and vegetarian bean-heavy bowls far from Lone Star orthodoxy.

timeline.event: San Antonio chili at Chicago World's Fair

teaching: Bloom dried chiles in hot oil 30 seconds before liquid — unlocks depth.
Simmer uncovered to reduce; skimming fat tames greasiness.
Day-two chili tastes better — flavors meld overnight.
fun_fact: Texas chili purists say no beans. The rest of America politely ignores them.
